title: Perf pulse - hypothesis handoff and micro-surge notes
content:
Perf pulse sync — 2026-11-17
Attendees: Aisha P. (owner), Daniel K., Sofia M., Evan B., Maya S., Tom L. (observability drop-in)
Objectives: share latest micro-surge findings, hand off prioritized hypotheses to bench team, agree on short shadow-run plan and config deltas to validate mitigation strategies.

1) Quick summary / context
- This week we saw repeated small latency spikes (~95th -> 99.9th) during batch-size transitions when QPS ramps from 35 -> 90 over ~20s in the Canary cluster. Not the large microburst we had in April, but persistent and correlated with KV-cache churn on long-running sessions.
- Impact: For a handful of customers on Dedicated, tail latency breaches observed for 3–7 minutes during scheduled traffic ramps. No request loss, but noticeable SLA noise.

2) Data snapshots shared in meeting
- Canary run (11/15): median p50 42ms, p95 128ms, p99.9 1.2s for seq_len=512 mixed workload.
- Heap / GC strobing seen on host gpu-node-14: increase in jemalloc stats coinciding with circuit breaker evictions.
- KV-cache hit-rate dip: from 87% -> 62% during ramp; cold misses increased by ~2.5x.
- Threadstarvation signal: a small uptick in scheduler queue depth (avg 7 -> 15) right before p99.9 spikes.

3) New observations since Friday
- When we artificially slowed the scheduler quantum to 6ms -> 3ms in shadow, the p99.9 spikes reduced but overall throughput dropped ~6%. Indicates a tradeoff between fairness preemption and raw throughput.
- Disabling prefix-prefetch (experiment id: pref-2026-11-16-a) eliminated the KV churn but increased token decode cpu by ~4% — suggests prefetched data was causing thrash on eviction path.

4) Hypotheses (ranked) — these are being handed off for bench verification
H1: Scheduler preemption threshold too coarse during mixed-length seqs -> longer requests hold KV locks and cause eviction cascades.
H2: Prefetcher/anticipatory KV writes are colliding with background eviction resulting in temporary cache reorg and CPU stalls.
H3: Memory allocator fragmentation under mixed quantized model sizes increases GC jitter during ramp (jemalloc + tcmalloc interaction on our image).
H4: I/O burst from log-flush + metrics ingestion (observability write peaks) adding jitter to host swap/eviction path.

5) Experiments to run (assigned)
- E1 (scheduler-tune-shadow): run 3 shadow waves adjusting quantum to [2ms,4ms,8ms], record p50/p95/p99.9, throughput, and CPU steal. Owner: Daniel K. Deadline: 2026-11-20. Linked: github PR 1193 (scheduler heuristics).
- E2 (prefetch-toggle-matrix): matrix of prefetch on/off + prefetch batch size [16,32,64] across seq profiles; measure kv hit-rate and token CPU. Owner: Sofia M. Deadline: 2026-11-22.
- E3 (allocator-variant-smoke): benchmark with jemalloc tunables + tcmalloc off build; capture jemalloc stats and GC event traces. Owner: Evan B. Deadline: 2026-11-24.
- E4 (obs-write-throttle): floor observability payload to 10% sample during ramp window to test interference. Owner: Maya S. Deadline: 2026-11-20.

6) Short shadow-run plan (what we'll run next week)
- Run two 1h shadow waves in Canary region across 11/18–11/19: one with scheduler tweaks (E1) and one with prefetch matrix (E2). Use identical traffic replay harness (traffic-replay v0.9.2) and seed same session set.
- Produce flamegraphs for top 10 hosts and KV cache heatmap snapshots every 60s.
- Export a small trace bundle and tag with run id for bisecting.

7) Instrumentation / logging asks
- Add a short-lived KV eviction counter with LRU bucket id to logs (low overhead) — Aisha will open a short PR. Expected visibility: will help confirm if evictions are clustered to certain buckets.
- Increase jemalloc stats dump frequency for E3 runs to 5s to capture micro-jitter. Evan will coordinate with infra to push the build.

8) Risks / tradeoffs raised
- Scheduler tightening might reduce p99.9 but could harm throughput for high-concurrency workloads (seen ~6% drop). Need to find a middle value or adaptive policy.
- Turning off prefetch is safe but raises CPU cost; must validate customer cost impact before any permanent change.

9) Decisions / committed actions
- Immediate: run E1 and E2 as listed.
- Short term: if E1 at 4ms quantum reduces p99.9 by >40% with <4% throughput loss, plan a canary rollout to one Dedicated pool by 11/30. Decision owner: Aisha.
- Observability: enable eviction counter in canary builds for next two weeks.

10) Open questions for SRE / infra
- Are there kernel-level scheduling anomalies on our GPU host images that align with these timestamps? Tom to correlate host-kernel logs (ticket INF-2151).
- Can we temporarily increase node memory headroom in Canary pool to see if that dampens eviction churn? Evan to propose capacity change.

11) Notes to self / loose ideas (brainstormed in meeting)
- Consider a lightweight per-session KV pin for hot sessions that keeps a small working set pinned during ramps (research cost/complexity).
- Explore adaptive prefetch backoff when eviction rate passes threshold.

12) Next sync / cadence
- Async updates on experiment status in the #perf-pulse channel.
- Quick re-sync Friday 2026-11-20 10:30 PT for interim results from E1 and E4. Full review 2026-11-24 standup.

Action list (concise):
- Daniel K.: schedule E1 runs + attach run ids (due 11/20)
- Sofia M.: implement prefetch matrix harness + results table (due 11/22)
- Evan B.: allocator build + jemalloc frequency changes (due 11/24)
- Maya S.: obs throttle experiment + dashboards for eviction counter (due 11/20)
- Aisha P.: open KV-eviction-logging PR + coordinate canary rollout plan (due 11/19)

If anything obvious missing, flag on the doc or ping me in slack. Will drop run-ids and links as experiments complete.

Appendix (quick logs / commands):
- replay command used: traffic-replay --profile mixed-512 --ramp 20s --qps 90 --seed 20261115 --out run-20261115-canary
- jemalloc dump: MALLOC_CONF=stats_print:true,lg_chunk:22 ./serving-binary --bench-traffic
- scheduler PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1193

End.
